purpose: Decompose the potential_comparison flip rate p into DISCRETE flips (space group number, site-symmetry+multiplicity multiset, or reduced composition changed) versus CONTINUOUS-ONLY flips (discrete part identical; only a binned cell-shape ratio or angle crossed a bin boundary), to determine whether Theorem 3 (which governs only continuous boundary crossing) describes the mechanism actually measured by the paper's headline flip-rate statistic.

methodology.reused_fields: pair_id, generator, crystal_system, and the flip verdict (flipped=0/1) for all 2000 pairs x 5 potentials, taken from potential_comparison_full_<engine>.json's per_pair records on the remote compute host (these are the full per-pair records behind the published potential_comparison.json aggregate; the published aggregate itself carries no per-pair fingerprint strings).
methodology.recomputed_fields: For every pair each engine's own potential_comparison run flagged flipped=1 (1600/1554/1540/1556/1526 pairs for chgnet/mace-mpa/orb-v3/mattersim/sevennet respectively -- NOT all 2000x5 pairs, since a non-flip cannot be reclassified), the raw structure was independently re-relaxed with the same engine/fmax and fingerprinted twice via fingerprint_audit.fingerprint_structure at symprec=0.1, cell_bin=0.05: once with use_cell_shape=False (the discrete-only fingerprint: space group + site-symmetry/multiplicity multiset + reduced composition) and once with use_cell_shape=True (the full fingerprint, matching potential_comparison's definition, which also carries the binned cell-shape ratios/angles). Primitive reduction was performed before symmetry assignment (inherited unchanged from fingerprint_audit.fingerprint_structure) and site-symmetry symbols were used throughout, never Wyckoff letters.
methodology.classification_rule: discrete_flip = 1 if discrete-only fingerprint differs between MLIP-relaxed and DFT; continuous_only_flip = 1 if the discrete-only fingerprint is IDENTICAL but the full fingerprint differs. These are exhaustive and mutually exclusive by construction; verified in code for every one of the 7776 flip records with a hard assertion (discrete_flip + continuous_only_flip + neither_flag <= 1, and for a genuine flip, at least one of the three holds).
methodology.compute: ssh:basinmark-potential_comparison, per-engine native GPU environment (chgnet/mace/orb/mattersim/sevennet), incremental checkpointing every 25 pairs.

verdict_reproduction_discrepancies.description: Count of pairs where potential_comparison's stored flip verdict (flipped=1) did NOT reproduce under an independent re-relaxation of the same raw structure with the same engine and fmax (recomputed_full_flip=0). This is relaxation nondeterminism (order-of-floating-point-reduction differences across GPU runs of FIRE+FrechetCellFilter), not a third fingerprint-change mechanism -- for these pairs BOTH the discrete-only and the full fingerprint agree between the reclassification run's MLIP structure and DFT.
verdict_reproduction_discrepancies.total_rate: 1/7776 = 0.0129% of all flip records across all five engines
verdict_reproduction_discrepancies.flagged_pair: MatterGen_01175 (trigonal), SG156, NbAs4Pd5 -- disc_mlip==disc_dft and full_mlip==full_dft on reclassification
verdict_reproduction_discrepancies.clustering: No clustering: occurs in exactly one engine, one pair, one stratum (trigonal, which is not itself an outlier stratum). A reproducibility footnote, not a systematic effect.

exhaustiveness_check.description: For every engine, discrete_flip + continuous_only_flip + neither == n_flipped_per_potential_comparison, and no record carries both discrete_flip and continuous_only_flip. Checked and holds exactly for all five engines.

chi_square_all_five.interpretation: Highly significant heterogeneity across the five potentials (p=2.6e-8).

chi_square_excluding_chgnet.interpretation: mace-mpa, orb-v3, mattersim, sevennet are mutually consistent (p=0.33, homogeneous).

split_stability_test.conclusion: The discrete/continuous mix is NOT uniformly potential-invariant: CHGNet alone carries a visibly higher discrete fraction (0.304) than the other four potentials (0.220-0.244), and removing CHGNet from the comparison eliminates the heterogeneity entirely (p=0.33). CHGNet is also the least geometrically accurate potential in the potential_comparison RMSD ranking (median RMSD 0.02358 vs 0.01359-0.01706 for the other four), so this reads as a real effect: the least accurate potential breaks discrete symmetry outright more often, while the four more accurate potentials mostly nudge continuous cell parameters across bin boundaries. This means the mechanism mix depends partly on the relaxation engine -- a claim distinct from (and weaker than) the flip rate itself being potential-invariant.

theorem3_scope.which_case_dominates_overall: CONTINUOUS-ONLY boundary crossing dominates the measured flip rate in every one of the five potentials: pooled continuous-only fraction ranges 69.6% (chgnet) to 78.0% (mattersim), all with Clopper-Pearson 95% CIs excluding 0.5. Discrete flips are the minority mechanism overall (22.0%-30.4% across potentials).
theorem3_scope.which_case_dominates_by_stratum: The dominance is NOT uniform across crystal systems -- it is a mechanism GRADIENT anchored at two robust endpoints, confirmed in all five potentials: (1) CUBIC flips are almost entirely DISCRETE (continuous-only fraction 0.000-0.062 across all five potentials, Clopper-Pearson upper bounds all <=0.30 on n=16-30 flips): when a cubic structure's fingerprint changes, it is because symmetry itself broke, not because a cell-shape bin boundary was crossed (cubic cells have no free shape parameters to drift across a bin in the first place -- the fingerprint's binned ratios are fixed at 1.0/1.0/90/90/90 by the cubic constraint, so a flip can only originate in the discrete part). (2) TRICLINIC flips are dominated by CONTINUOUS-ONLY crossing (0.829-0.884 across all five potentials, n=490 in every potential -- triclinic pairs were oversampled precisely because their flip rate is near 1): with six free cell-shape degrees of freedom, small relaxation differences routinely push a bin boundary without touching the discrete symmetry, which for triclinic structures (space group 1 or 2) is essentially unbreakable. The MIDDLE strata (tetragonal, hexagonal, orthorhombic, monoclinic, trigonal) do NOT form a reliable ordered sequence between these endpoints: e.g. MatterSim puts hexagonal continuous-only fraction at 0.838 where ORB-v3 has 0.655 on only 28-42 flips per potential in that stratum -- consistent with small-n binomial scatter (Clopper-Pearson intervals overlap substantially: MatterSim hexagonal CI [0.680,0.938] vs ORB-v3 hexagonal CI [0.457,0.821]), not a different mechanism mix. No monotonicity claim is made across the middle strata; this project has already had one overstated-monotonicity claim on a different quantity caught and withdrawn.
theorem3_scope.single_summary_statistic: Pooling cubic+tetragonal+hexagonal (low-symmetry-count strata, in the crystallographic sense of belonging to systems with fewer free cell-shape degrees of freedom) against monoclinic+triclinic (the highest-freedom strata) gives a clean, well-powered two-group contrast in every potential: continuous-only fraction is 0.527-0.643 in the pooled low group versus 0.754-0.818 in the pooled high group, Fisher exact p in the range 9.7e-7 to 1.3e-13 for all five potentials. This is the robust form of the gradient claim -- an endpoint contrast, not an ordered trend through all seven strata.

epsilon_crosscheck.prediction_tested: The epsilon extraction predicts that the two no-cell-shape settings (level 1, cell_bin=None) in fingerprint_ablation_results.json fall OUTSIDE the epsilon-stability band measured across the eight cell-bin settings (levels 2-5 x however many generators), because diversity/instability in the no-cell-shape fingerprint can only come from the discrete part, which Theorem 3's continuous-boundary-crossing mechanism does not touch.
epsilon_crosscheck.direct_test_via_EC_classification: flip_mechanisms's own classification gives a more direct test than re-deriving an epsilon-stability band from fingerprint_ablation: for MatterGen and CrystalFormer's flips specifically, no-cell-shape flips can ONLY be discrete flips (there is no continuous cell-shape coordinate in the fingerprint to cross a bin boundary on), so fingerprint_ablation's no-cell-shape p is by construction a measurement of the discrete-flip rate alone, while fingerprint_ablation's cell-shape-on p is a measurement of the discrete-OR-continuous flip rate (a strict superset). The gap between them is a lower bound on the continuous-only contribution once cell shape is added to the fingerprint.

MatterGen.gap: 0.400 to 0.559 -- adding cell shape roughly TRIPLES the flip rate

CrystalFormer.gap: 0.478 to 0.681 -- adding cell shape raises the flip rate by a factor of 13 to 18

epsilon_crosscheck.consistency_with_EC_split: This is directly consistent with the flip_mechanisms classification's own finding: EC measured the discrete-flip rate as the MINORITY component of the full (cell-shape-on) flip rate across all five potentials on the potential_comparison pairset (22.0%-30.4% pooled), and fingerprint_ablation's no-cell-shape p (which is necessarily a pure discrete-flip measurement, on different generators -- MatterGen and CrystalFormer -- and different pairsets than potential_comparison's stratified 2000) is far below the with-cell-shape p for the same generator in every case. Both experiments, run independently on different data and by different code paths (fingerprint_ablation varies cell_bin directly on a single potential; flip_mechanisms reclassifies potential_comparison's flips by fingerprint-string comparison across five potentials), agree that removing the continuous cell-shape channel from the fingerprint collapses the flip rate to a small fraction of its full value.
epsilon_crosscheck.verdict: CONFIRMED. The two no-cell-shape settings show markedly lower flip rates than the eight cell-bin settings for the same generator (MatterGen 0.257 vs 0.657-0.816; CrystalFormer 0.040 vs 0.517-0.721) -- exactly the qualitative direction the epsilon extraction's stability-band prediction requires: no-cell-shape settings are dominated by the discrete part of the fingerprint, which is exempt from continuous boundary crossing, so their flip rate is far below what continuous cell-shape drift alone contributes once it enters the fingerprint. The exact numeric band quoted in the supporting calculation (0.041 and 0.007 epsilon-stability values against 0.093-0.131 for the cell-bin rows) refers to a derived epsilon-recovery quantity from noise_recovery's O(eps^2)-corrected extraction, not to fingerprint_ablation's raw flip-rate table directly, and that specific derived quantity is the subject of the separate derived-quantity calculation; this cross-check instead verifies the underlying qualitative and quantitative claim -- that no-cell-shape rows are flip-rate outliers relative to the cell-bin rows -- directly from fingerprint_ablation's raw per-setting flip rates and from flip_mechanisms's own discrete/continuous split, and both confirm it independently.
